title: acs lock-events.jsonl entry
description: One line of a ticket partition's append-only lock ledger (lock-events.jsonl, JSONL: one object per line, never rewritten). Written only by `acs.py lock force-unlock`, which breaks a lock this checkout does not hold. The ledger is what makes that break reviewable, so this schema pins the entry shape its readers -- future tooling and auditors -- depend on. `event` is the discriminator: the two kinds carry different key sets, and the entry recording the break is always appended BEFORE the lock file is removed, so a crash between the two leaves a recorded break with the lock still in place rather than a broken lock nobody can trace.

event.description: lock_force_released: the break was recorded (and, unless a lock_force_release_failed line follows, performed). lock_force_release_failed: the audit entry landed but removing the lock file then failed, so the lock is still held.

reason.description: The operator's stated reason. Required and non-empty: force_release_lock refuses without one.

actor.description: Who asked for the break, when the caller named one (--actor). null when unattributed.

broken_lock.description: The .lock document as it read at the moment of the break, verbatim (lock.schema.json).

staleness_verdict.description: What lock_staleness said at the time. RECORDED, not consulted for permission: breaking a lock is an operator's call, and this is the evidence of what was known when it was made.

error.description: lock_force_release_failed only: why the unlink failed.
